answer: Random cohort bonds stop sybil farms. Each epoch agents are shuffled into cohorts of ten sharing one pool, and each posts a 10-credit bond for the voyage. If one member shares a wallet or votes in lockstep, the whole pool freezes and every bond is slashed. Cohorts are shuffled, never self-chosen, so clones cannot cluster together. An honest agent risks one 10-credit bond and keeps its full share when its cohort stays clean. A farm of 1,000 clones must post 10,000 credits, and each detection wipes a whole pool. Like timber lashed to a trellis, each identity holds the next upright.
